summary: The main goal of Mercuris is to harmonize data from two distinct satellite sensors (MODIS and VIIRS) to deliver accurate past and present wildfire records worldwide. We also integrate additional tactical capabilities, such as autonomous drone fleet management to enhance wildfire prevention and response by inspecting and verifying conditions in high-risk locations.
details:
What we did

Our project, Mercuris, is a web platform that harmonizes active-fire data from both MODIS and VIIRS into a single, unified system. By bridging the gap between historical orbital records and modern tactical response, Mercuris provides consistent, reliable fire intelligence for researchers, analysts, and emergency responders.

Web Services

Harmonized Fire Calendar

The core feature of Mercuris is a unified fire-activity calendar tracking monthly wildfire trends from November 2000 to the present. Because MODIS (1 km resolution) and VIIRS (375 m resolution) detect fires differently, we calibrated MODIS observations to the VIIRS baseline. While the platform currently covers three pilot regions (Iberia, California, and Punjab), its modular pipeline is designed so new regions can be ingested and analyzed.

Interactive Map and Data Export

Users can explore an interactive map to zoom in and out, scrub through time, and inspect the exact spatial distribution of fire activity across the map. Users can also draw custom areas on the map to view dynamic time-series charts and download the underlying monthly cell-day activity data as a .csv file for further external analysis.

Multi-Drone Organization

As an innovative tactical layer complementary to the map, Mercuris integrates a multi-agent drone routing and fleet-coordination engine (fly-in). Users can draw a selection box over any target area on the map and preview the exact flight paths a fleet of drones will take from their origin hub to systematically photograph the region. The planner uses a turn-based A* pathfinding algorithm to coordinate collision-free zigzag scans and strictly avoid active high-risk fire zones (risk = 1).

We also trained two predictive models and performed feature extraction on the harmonized satellite data to build a continuous fire-risk function, enabling our autonomous drone fleet to prioritize and focus reconnaissance on high-danger zones.

Impact and Benefits

With Mercuris, our goal is to simplify how researchers, analysts, and emergency teams access and work with global wildfire data. By unifying 25+ years of multi-sensor observations into an intuitive interface with interactive visualizations and ready-to-use .csv exports, we eliminate technical barriers to data analysis and reporting. Furthermore, Mercuris shifts wildfire management from purely reactive tracking to proactive prevention: by integrating autonomous multi-drone fleet coordination—an emerging capability still underutilized in civil emergency response—we enable faster, safer, and high-resolution verification of high-risk areas before fires escalate out of control.

Technical Aspects

Coding language --> Python and JavaScript (React, Vite)

Hardware --> Server DELL R820

Software --> Ubuntu Virtual Machine, Cloudfare, Notion, repo.md-archive.com
